Hi Amanda — thanks for the roster and the clear ask. Short answer: we treat the committed retainer and the escalation roster as two linked but separable levers. In practice there are three approaches we offer depending on how BrightCart wants to balance cost vs guaranteed response: 

1) Fixed retainer + flat uptime bands (default): retainer covers guaranteed weekday response & escalation routing. Uptime credits are based on observed uptime against the committed SLA and do not change based on roster headcount. This is simplest for procurement.

2) Roster-linked retainer (recommended for smaller weekend coverage): retainer discounts if you accept a smaller guaranteed headcount after-hours. Example: if weekend guaranteed on-call decreases from 4 -> 2 engineers, retainer is discounted by 12–18% (depending on response window). Uptime credit slabs still measured against the SLO, but the credit cap is adjusted proportionally to the guaranteed coverage.

3) Tiered escalation supplement: keep full retainer; add an on-demand escalation supplement hourly fee for outside-window paging that automatically converts to credits if used above X incidents/month. This is good if you expect bursts but want predictable baseline spend.

I'll loop in Naomi to confirm the credit cap math and Marissa to check how this affects pricing bands and discounting for the BR-4382 deal. If you have a preference, we can draft the SOW text and example numbers.

Jordan Blake

Redwood Inference

Amanda — thanks for patience while we modeled this. We've put together two concrete, clean options so procurement and SRE can pick based on whether predictability or lowest baseline cost is the priority. I've attached the SOW excerpt and the anonymous roster with the two scenarios computed.

Option A — Simplicity (Flat retainer + standard uptime bands)
- Retainer: $40,000 / month (covers weekday + standard weekend triage routing)
- Uptime credit: standard slab (0.5% credit per 1% shortfall, capped at 30% of monthly retainer)
- Pros: simplest invoicing; no change to credit math
- Cons: higher monthly cost if you don’t need full weekend headcount

Option B — Roster-linked (Discounted retainer + proportional credit cap) [Recommended if you accept smaller guaranteed weekend headcount]
- Retainer: $34,000 / month (15% discount reflecting reduced guaranteed weekend headcount)
- Uptime credit: same slab structure, but credit payout cap is prorated for weekend-only incidents (we cap weekend-only incident credit payout at 50% of the standard monthly credit cap)
- Add-on: Out-of-window escalation supplement: $350 / incident after the first 5 out-of-window incidents per month (converts to credits if >20 incidents/month)
- Pros: lower baseline bill; predictable exposure on weekends
- Cons: more line-items in SOW and invoicing

Next steps: if BrightCart prefers Option B I’ll update the SOW language (attached) to include the roster definition, guaranteed headcount table, and the credit cap formula. If you prefer A we’ll leave the standard SLA text and proceed to signature.

Please reply with preferred option and whether procurement wants the credit math in a CSV (we can generate a worst-case simulation).
